code: refused <- tryCatch(   flexybayes(yield ~ env, random = ~ fa(env, 2):gen, data = dat,              backend = "inla", verbose = FALSE),   error = function(e) e ) cat(conditionMessage(refused)) #> fa(env, 2):gen requests a factor-analytic covariance -- a rank-k loading matrix plus a diagonal. Neither active engine emits one: INLA's f() has no factor-analytic latent model, and brms group-level effects are either uncorrelated or fully unstructured. Use us(env):gen for the full unstructured covariance, diag(env):gen for heterogeneous variances with no correlation, or ASReml for the factor-analytic model itself. The term still parses, so fb_terms() will describe it. class(refused)[1:3] #> [1] "flexybayes_refusal_fa_not_representable" #> [2] "flexybayes_refusal"                      #> [3] "error"

text: M covariance carrier. type = "blocks" base-R list K square covariance matrices; otherwise square numeric matrix (base-R Matrix). Inside formula argument names matrix resolved known_matrices. type Character(1): carrier type, one "dense", "chol", "precision", "blocks", "low_rank". title: Construct a structured-covariance carrier — fb_cov
text: carrier's type selects downstream emit path derives covariance square root. "dense" takes lower Cholesky supplied covariance; "chol" uses supplied factor directly; "precision" inverts via Cholesky precision matrix; "blocks" assembles block-diagonal covariance list per-block matrices; "low_rank" pairs rank-K factor registered approximation scheme (reserved v0.4.0 – carrier vocabulary active validated, approximate-covariance fit route activates subsequent release). Inside model formula carrier written inline – matrix argument names matrix passed known_matrices, exactly legacy keyword forms . construction-time check light structural probe (shape, lower-triangular pattern, symmetry, block count); full level-aware validation runs fit time grouping factor.

text: Fit cell-aggregatable mixed model dataset held disk, reading row-range chunks accumulating exact per-cell sufficient statistics rather materialising full table memory. method scales cell count K (number distinct factor design combinations), row count N. replicated factorial design collapses billions rows thousand cells fits seconds; design keys continuous covariate compress refused chunk read. Continuous fixed effects, random slopes, structured covariance, smooth terms break cell-constant linear-predictor property likewise refused – pass data flexybayes() per row models. Supported families "gaussian" (identity link), "binomial", "poisson". binomial data supply trials name column trial counts (0/1 response treated Bernoulli one trial per row). poisson data supply exposure name exposure / offset column.

title: Fit a mixed model to an out-of-core dataset by streaming aggregation — flexybayes_stream
text: Max Moldovan, max.moldovan@adelaide.edu.au

title: Fit a mixed model to an out-of-core dataset by streaming aggregation — flexybayes_stream
code: if (FALSE) { # interactive() && requireNamespace("fst", quietly = TRUE) # The fit runs on INLA, which is distributed from its own repository # rather than from CRAN, so the guard keeps the example readable on a # machine that does not carry it. if (requireNamespace("INLA", quietly = TRUE)) {   set.seed(1L)   n <- 1e6   df <- data.frame(     env = factor(sample(letters[1:6], n, replace = TRUE)),     geno = factor(sample(1:50, n, replace = TRUE)),     y = rnorm(n)   )   path <- tempfile(fileext = ".fst")   fst::write_fst(df, path)   fit <- flexybayes_stream(y ~ env, random = ~ geno, source = path,                            backend = "inla")   summary(fit) } }
